newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates slip on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates slip on low demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates slipped on Wednesday as sharp rises in previous sessions induced spinners to buy cautiously, dealers said.

They said prices were likely to remain steady to weak following the official announcement that the 1996/97 (July-June) crop will be above nine million 375-lb bales, against an earlier target of 10 million and 1995/96 output of 9.96 million bales.
"Spinners kept quiet as prices have risen very sharply, though speculation about the size of the crop has not ended," dealer Nasim Usman said.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,350 rupees ($58.42) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
